_comment: md-zero-2026-08-11 PLAN.md Phase 7's own zero-rule gate (check-no-markdown-reads.py) needs an
explicit exemption list, in tension with the plan's literal 'zero allowlist entries' line --
resolved in favour of this list after a real risk audit (asked of the user, recorded in the
session) found the plan's premise false: only 10 of 287 tracked .md files are rendered from a
registry, so deleting the scripts that VALIDATE the other 277 (link integrity, doc
classification, script-mention verification, download-link pinning, hardcoded-path scanning)
would remove real, working protection with nothing to replace it.
PLAN-11-to-4.md (same day) then cut this from 11 to 6: check-doc-inventory.py never actually
needed the exemption (pure path enumeration, proven by removing it and re-running the scanner);
the 3 doc generators' --check modes stopped reading their own committed output back (staleness
detection moved to `git diff --exit-code` in their callers instead); run-script-inventory-check.ps1
replaced whole-repo prose-scanning with an explicit documentedIn declaration per script; and
run-maturity-max-roadmap-boundary-check.ps1's entire external-roadmap-file read was deleted
outright (a machine-local personal path that could only ever verify on one laptop -- a control
not worth keeping, not a coupling worth converting).
THE DISTINCTION THIS LIST DRAWS: a script that mines markdown prose as an unstructured DATA
SOURCE feeding program logic or a generated artifact (RAG indexing, CLI command extraction,
policy assertions parsed from prose) is the actual defect class Groups B-G fixed -- there are
zero of those left, and none belong on this list. A script whose entire job IS validating
markdown prose itself (because that prose is hand-authored and nothing else guarantees its
correctness) is a different, legitimate thing: a linter. Every entry below is a linter.
Every entry requires a non-empty `why` (check-doc-inventory.py's R4 discipline, the same this
repo already applies to every other allowlist -- security-pattern-sweep-allowlist.json,
twin-pair-registry.json). R3-equivalent: an entry naming a file that no longer exists must be
removed in the same commit that removes the file.

exemptFiles.why: The only link-integrity check in the repo: walks every tracked .md and verifies relative links resolve. 277 of 287 tracked docs are hand-authored, not generated from any registry, so nothing else catches a broken link in them.

Classifies every docs/**/*.md by path pattern (JSON-driven) and verifies script/report paths mentioned in doc prose still exist. 134 of 144 scanned documents are hand-authored; this is the only thing catching a stale script-path mention in them.
Test harness for run-doc-entrypoint-validation.ps1 above; its fixtures are .md files by necessity, same exemption.

md-zero-2026-08-11 PLAN.md Phase 3 already narrowed this from a 94-file sweep to 3 declared knownLinkSites (scripts/policy/release-download-links.json) -- but verifying a download link has not drifted to a pinned version still means reading those 3 real files' actual text. No registry generates README.md/docs/MANAGER.md/docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md, so this is the only thing catching a hand-typed pinned link.

Scans NPDevCli/**/*.md (among other extensions) for hardcoded drive-letter paths (REG-144). The .md files under NPDevCli are hand-authored, not generated, and a hardcoded path IN the doc's prose is itself the defect this check exists to catch -- there is no registry to move the assertion into.
